I'll run LedgerMind's analysis over your intents.
**Verdict: the spending is fine — the authorisation isn't.** Risk level: medium.

Your agent has spent only **1.28 USDC across 4 payments**, all receipted, all to allowlisted merchants. Nothing looks like leakage. The problem is that **67 USDC of authority** is sitting behind that 1.28 USDC of actual use.

**Two things to fix now:**

1. **Unrestricted 10 USDC intent — `0x5682…2f5b`** ("General ops agent - discretionary spend"). It has an *empty merchant allowlist*, meaning the agent can pay **any address**, up to 2 USDC per tx / 10 USDC total. It has made **zero payments** in the window. Either name the merchants it's meant to pay (`restrictMerchants`) or revoke it and pull back the 0.30 USDC funded. Dormant open-ended authority is the worst exposure here.

2. **Stranded cash — `0xe88b…df16`** (Marketing tools trial, revoked: "Trial ended, tool not adopted"). Funded 1.00 USDC, spent 0.20, so **0.80 USDC is stuck** on an intent that can never spend again. `withdrawRemainder` recovers it with zero downside.

**Two worth doing this week:**

3. **`0x4e08…bcf4`** (Cloud infra autopay) — both payments landed at **0.49 USDC against a 0.50 per-tx cap (98%), seconds apart, same merchant `0x1111…1111`**. That's the cap clipping or splitting a real invoice. It's also burned 49% of its 2 USDC total cap on day one of a 30-day term, so it will likely bind early. Raise the per-tx cap — but size it to an actual invoice amount, not a guess.

4. **`0xb530…7ca7`** (Research subscriptions) — 50 USDC cap against 0.10 USDC spent. That's 75% of all your authorisation supporting 8% of spend. Allowlist is properly scoped to one merchant, so blast radius is contained, but the headroom is unearned. Cut it.

**Caveats worth knowing:** the 90-day window contains only **one day of activity** (2026-09-13), so there's no real baseline to judge "normal" against. Merchant addresses are unlabelled — I can't confirm `0x1111…1111` is actually your cloud provider. And I can't tell whether those two 0.49 USDC payments are one split invoice or two genuine charges, which is exactly what determines how far to raise that cap.

Data is current — indexed block 270808905 on Sei Atlantic, no indexing errors.

data.headline: Spending itself is disciplined and fully receipted (1.28 USDC across 4 payments), but 67 USDC of authorisation is backing it — including a 10 USDC unrestricted-merchant intent that has never paid anyone and 0.80 USDC stranded on a revoked intent.

findings.title: Idle capital sitting on a revoked intent
findings.detail: 0xe88b…df16 (Marketing tools trial) was revoked with reason 'Trial ended, tool not adopted' after a single 0.20 USDC payment, but 1.00 USDC was funded and 0.80 USDC remains unspent. Revoked intents cannot spend, so this is pure stranded capital recoverable via withdrawRemainder.
evidence: state=Revoked, revokeReason='Trial ended, tool not adopted'

findings.title: Active 10 USDC intent with an empty (unrestricted) merchant allowlist
findings.detail: 0x5682…2f5b ('General ops agent - discretionary spend') is Active with totalCap 10 USDC, perTxCap 2 USDC, merchantAllowlistSize 0 and unrestrictedMerchants=true. It has made zero payments in the whole window. An unbounded-destination intent is the single largest containment risk in this set: the agent could pay any address up to 2 USDC per tx, 10 USDC total, with no demonstrated need for the authority. Only 0.30 USDC is funded today, which limits present-day loss, but the authorisation stands ready for any future top-up.

findings.title: Cloud infra agent is being throttled by its per-tx cap
findings.detail: Both payments on 0x4e08…bcf4 landed at 0.49 USDC against a 0.50 USDC perTxCap — 98% of cap, twice in a row, seconds apart, to the same merchant 0x1111…1111. That pattern is consistent with the cap clipping or splitting real invoices rather than sizing them. It has also burned 49% of its 2 USDC total cap in a single day against a purpose described as 'weekly' autopay, so the total cap is likely to bind before the 30-day term ends.
evidence: purpose: 'Cloud infra autopay - GPU + storage, weekly'

findings.title: Research intent is over-authorised by roughly 250x observed spend
findings.detail: 0xb530…7ca7 carries a 50 USDC total cap — 75% of all authorisation in the account — against 0.10 USDC of actual spend (capUsedPct 0.2) and one payment at 2% of its 5 USDC perTxCap. The allowlist is properly scoped to one merchant, so the blast radius is contained, but the headroom is unjustified by behaviour.

findings.title: Hygiene is good where it counts: every payment is receipted and on-allowlist
findings.detail: All 4 payments carry hasReceipt=true and every spending intent except the dormant ops intent has a 1-merchant allowlist. Merchant concentration (0x1111…1111 at 0.98 of 1.28 USDC) matches the stated infra purpose rather than indicating leakage.

actions.rationale: Intent is already Revoked and can never spend again; 0.80 USDC of the 1.00 USDC funded is stranded. This is the only immediately recoverable capital in the account and carries no downside.

A 10 USDC / 2 USDC-per-tx Active intent with an empty allowlist can pay any address. It has made zero payments in 90 days, so there is no operational cost to naming the merchants it is actually meant to pay. If no merchant can be named, revoke it instead and withdraw the 0.30 USDC funded — dormant discretionary authority is the worst kind.

Two consecutive payments at 98% of the 0.50 USDC perTxCap to a single allowlisted infra merchant indicate the cap is mis-sized and may be forcing invoice splitting. Raising perTxCap is low-risk here because the allowlist is a single merchant and the 2 USDC total cap remains the real ceiling — but size the increase to a known invoice amount, not a guess.

50 USDC authorised against 0.10 USDC spent is 75% of total account authorisation supporting 8% of spend. Cutting the cap to a few multiples of observed use removes the largest single block of unused authority without affecting the one merchant it pays.

dataGaps: The window is labelled 90 days but all 4 payments and all dailySpend rows fall on a single day (2026-09-13), so there is no real trend, cadence, or baseline to judge 'normal' spend against.
Merchant addresses are unlabelled — I cannot confirm 0x1111…1111 is a legitimate cloud provider or that 0x3333…3333 matched the marketing trial's intended vendor.

No invoice or expected-amount data, so I cannot confirm whether the two 0.49 USDC payments on 0x4e08…bcf4 are a split of one larger charge or two genuine separate charges; this determines how far to raise perTxCap.
No information on which merchants the 'General ops agent - discretionary spend' intent was meant to pay, so restrict_merchants cannot be pre-populated.

fundedUsdc is far below totalCapUsdc on every intent (0.3–1.2 vs 2–50); the funding mechanism and whether top-ups are automatic is unknown, which changes how much real exposure the large caps represent.
